title: Grave Team Six
text:
Overview
Grave Team Six fuses two mechanics into one engine: Fathomless descent (your graveyard’s permanent count X makes creatures huge and spells brutal) and Teamwork (tap creatures with total power N to unlock the second mode of a spell). The bridge between the two is Souls of the Lost — its power literally equals the number of permanent cards in your graveyard, which makes it the perfect creature to tap for Teamwork costs, over and over again.
Every fetchland, surveil land, looting artifact, and mill spell in the deck doubles as fuel: each permanent in the graveyard makes Souls bigger, makes Terror Tide and Chupacabra Echo wipe harder, lets Squirming Emergence reanimate bigger things, and turns Matzalantli’s back face — the land The Core — into a mana engine. Teamwork spells then convert that giant board presence into reanimation, removal, counterspells, and a 6/5 hexproof Leviathan.

title: Grave Team Six

Approach

Game plan phases

Dig (turns 1-3). Play fetchlands and crack them, surveil with Undercity Sewers / Hedge Maze / Underground Mortuary, cast Cache Grab or Song of Stupefaction to mill, and loot with Matzalantli, the Great Door. Every permanent that hits the graveyard counts.
Grow (turns 3-5). Souls of the Lost becomes a 5/6 or 6/7. Tap it (and Solemn Simulacrum or Chupacabra Echo) to pay Teamwork costs: Too Evil to Stay Dead reanimates anything, Cruel Alliance exiles any creature and gains life, We Say Thee Nay! hard-counters, Go Nuts! fights and pumps.
Win (turn 5+). Reanimate with Squirming Emergence and Earth’s Mightiest Heroes, clear the board with Terror Tide (Souls survives as X+1 toughness), then kill with Rogue’s Passage plus a giant Souls, Season of Loss draining for your creature count, or the hexproof Leviathan.

title: Grave Team Six
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Prioritize a fetchland or surveil land on turn one. Turn two, either Souls of the Lost (discard a redundant land) or Song of Stupefaction / Cache Grab to start the graveyard. Do not hold back graveyard fuel — X grows fast, and every point matters for Souls, Terror Tide, and Squirming Emergence.


Mid game
With four or five permanents in the graveyard, Souls is a real threat and Teamwork costs are trivial to pay. Reanimate a Solemn Simulacrum to ramp and draw, or loop Matzalantli for card selection. Use Cruel Alliance and Chupacabra Echo to keep the opponent’s board small while your graveyard grows.


The combo turn

Graveyard has 10+ permanents: Souls of the Lost is an 11/12.
Tap Souls plus one other creature to cast Too Evil to Stay Dead with Teamwork — return the best creature card in your graveyard (often another Souls or Solemn).
Cast Squirming Emergence (X = 10+): return Matzalantli or a creature.
Attack: activate Rogue’s Passage on Souls. 11+ unblockable damage, often lethal. If they survive, Terror Tide next turn clears everything while Souls survives as X+1 toughness.



Win condition 2: Season of Loss and the Leviathan
Season of Loss with {P}{P}{P} makes each opponent lose life equal to the number of creature cards in your graveyard — commonly 8 to 12. The {P} mode forces sacrifices to clear blockers, and {P}{P} refills your hand if creatures died this turn. Atlantis Attacks (cast with Teamwork) creates a 6/5 hexproof Leviathan and bounces two permanents — a resilient finisher that dodges spot removal. Restless Reef and Restless Vinestalk close out games when the opponent is low.


Mulligan guide
Keep: two to three lands, plus any of Souls of the Lost, Cache Grab, Song of Stupefaction, Matzalantli, or a reanimation spell. A hand with no graveyard fuel and no two-drop is a mulligan. Ship hands full of six- and seven-mana spells. Lands that surveil or fetch count as fuel, so land-heavy hands are better here than in most decks.


Key interactions and edge cases

Souls of the Lost survives your own Terror Tide: toughness is X+1, so a board wipe leaves your biggest creature standing.
Matzalantli transforms with four or more permanent types (artifact, creature, enchantment, land, planeswalker, battle) in the graveyard — the deck naturally has artifact (Matzalantli, fetchlands), creature, land, and enchantment types.
Teamwork taps as an additional cost: tap creatures before the spell resolves, so removal in response does not stop the second mode.
Cache Grab mills four and returns a permanent card to hand — instant speed, and it is both fuel and recursion in one card.
Insidious Roots: every reanimation makes a Plant, then pumps all Plants; Plants also tap for mana, creating a late-game army that pays Teamwork costs.
Graveyard hate (exile effects) is the deck’s main weakness: fetchlands and mill still work, but keep Cache Grab and draw spells for resilience.



Matchups

Aggro: Terror Tide, Chupacabra Echo, and Cruel Alliance keep the board clear; Souls blocks well. Prioritize graveyard count over speed.
Midrange: win the value war — reanimation loops out-grind most midrange decks; Solemn Simulacrum and Squirming Emergence provide card advantage.
Control: We Say Thee Nay! protects key spells; Atlantis Attacks and recursion from the graveyard are hard for control to answer permanently. Rogue’s Passage turns any surviving creature into a clock.

title: Spiderweb Landslide
text:
Overview
Spiderweb Landslide is the tenth dedicated daily Hobbit combo deck. Nine earlier builds claimed the set’s headline engines — the goblin amass raid, the dwarven companies, the elvenking’s court, Smaug’s hoard, the wilderland pack, the Lake-town recruits, the mountain musicians, the crooked thieves and the Mirkwood menagerie — leaving exactly four Hobbit cards unused, and this deck plays all four of them: Old Fat Spider, Mirkwood Meditator, Eagle’s Rescue and Front Porch Sentries. The remaining usable Hobbit pool is only four cards, so the deck is fused around the mechanic those leftovers share — Landfall — and filled with Standard support that turns that mechanic into a burn combo.
The engine is a chain of landfall triggers. Mirkwood Meditator swings as a 4/2 every time a land enters; Spitfire Lagac pings each opponent for 1; Tatyova, Benthic Druid turns every land drop into a card; Genemorph Imago turns any creature into a 6/6; Felidar Retreat makes cats or anthems. Springbloom Druid and Arid Archway generate extra land drops per turn, and Twinflame Tyrant doubles every point of damage the engine produces. The second, fully independent win is voltron: Old Fat Spider — a 6/7 with reach that can’t be blocked by power 2 or less and draws a card whenever an opponent targets it — carries Eagle’s Rescue, With Great Power . . ., Ethereal Armor, Angelic Destiny and friends into a flying, first-strike, hexproof kill, again doubled by the Tyrant.

title: Spiderweb Landslide
text:
Approach

Game plan by phase

Spin the web (turns 1–3). Ethereal Armor, Fae Flight or Fungal Fortitude on turn 1–2; Mirkwood Meditator (2/4) or Front Porch Sentries on turn 2; Genemorph Imago or Springbloom Druid on turn 3. Springbloom Druid ramps and double-triggers landfall immediately (sacrifice a land, put two basics in tapped).
Catch the draft (turns 3–5). Spitfire Lagac on turn 4 turns every land drop into damage; Tatyova, Benthic Druid turns every land drop into a card; Felidar Retreat turns land drops into cats or counters. Arid Archway loops a land back to hand for a bonus trigger each turn.
Landslide (turns 5+). Twinflame Tyrant doubles everything. Each land drop now pings for 2; each cat token hits for 4; Old Fat Spider attacks for 24+. Niv-Mizzet, Visionary turns every ping into a card so the loop keeps finding lands.

title: Spiderweb Landslide
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Mirkwood Meditator on turn 2 is the ideal start — a 2/4 that blocks everything in the format’s early game and becomes a 4/2 on your first landfall. Front Porch Sentries trades and shrinks a blocker on the way out. Ethereal Armor on the Meditator makes a 3/4 first-striker that only grows. Play your basics first; the tapped duals enter on later turns when the tempo cost is smaller.


Mid game
Resolve landfall engines in order: Spitfire Lagac (damage), then Tatyova (cards), then Felidar Retreat (board). Each land drop from here on produces damage, a card, and a body simultaneously. Arid Archway adds a free extra trigger every turn: let it bounce a basic, then replay the basic. Genemorph Imago turns the 1/1 Springbloom Druid or a cat token into a 6/6 to attack through.


The combo turn

Board: Spitfire Lagac + Twinflame Tyrant (+ Niv-Mizzet, Visionary ideally).
Chain: play Springbloom Druid — sacrifice a land, two basics enter, two landfall triggers: 4 damage (doubled), two cards from Niv, two life from Tatyova.
Loop: Arid Archway enters, bounces a land, {C}{C}; replay the land: another 2 damage, another card.
Convert: every card Niv draws is another chance to find lands; Genemorph makes a 6/6; Felidar Retreat’s cats are 2/2s that hit for 4 with the Tyrant. A six-land turn ends the game.



Win condition 2 — the giant Spider
Suit up Old Fat Spider: Eagle’s Rescue (+2/+2 flying), With Great Power . . . (+2/+2 per aura), Ethereal Armor (+1/+1 per enchantment, first strike), Angelic Destiny (+4/+4 flying first strike), Fae Flight (hexproof on entry), Fungal Fortitude (recurrence). At five auras the Spider attacks as a 16/17 flying first-striker; Twinflame Tyrant doubles the damage to 32. Its own text makes it a nightmare to answer: it can’t be blocked by power 2 or less, and any opponent spell or ability that targets it draws you a card. With Great Power . . . also redirects all damage to it, and Angelic Destiny + Eagle’s Rescue + Fungal Fortitude recur the whole package from the graveyard.


Mulligan guide

Keep: 2–3 lands including a green source, a two-drop, and ideally Mirkwood Meditator or Springbloom Druid.
Ship: one-landers, six-land hands, and hands with the double-red Tyrant or double-white Angelic Destiny but no matching source.
Prefer hands with an engine (Lagac, Tatyova, Felidar Retreat) on a playable curve.
An opening of three ETB-tapped duals is a mulligan — you need basics early.



Key interactions and edge cases

Twinflame Tyrant doubles damage from any source you control — landfall pings, cat-token triggers, and Old Fat Spider’s combat damage all double. It does not double life loss.
Genemorph Imago sets base P/T, so it overrides Mirkwood Meditator’s 4/2 landfall option — target the Meditator only when you want 6/6, and don’t expect the 4/2 to stick.
Eagle’s Rescue recurs onto power 1 or less creatures — the natural target is Springbloom Druid (1/1), giving you a 3/3 flying ramp druid.
Fungal Fortitude returns the creature tapped — the Spider comes back tapped, so activate it before combat or accept the delay; the aura stays attached.
Fae Flight’s hexproof is until end of turn — cast it in response to removal, not preemptively.
Angelic Destiny returns to hand, not the battlefield — when the Spider dies, the Destiny goes back to hand while Fungal Fortitude brings the Spider back; both layers of protection work together.
Arid Archway’s bounce is mandatory — always bounce a basic you can replay; if you bounced a Desert (Arid Archway itself or another), you surveil 1.
Maelstrom’s colored mana only casts Dragon or Omen spells — use it for Twinflame Tyrant and Niv-Mizzet, Visionary; don’t hold it for Lagac.
Niv-Mizzet, Visionary draws per point of noncombat damage — a doubled 2-damage ping draws 2 cards; the draw triggers after the damage resolves.



Matchups

Aggro: Meditator’s 2/4 and the Sentries’ death-shrink hold the ground; Ethereal Armor turns any blocker into a first-strike wall; Tatyova’s life-gain and the life-gain duals buy the turn needed for the combo.
Midrange: the landfall engine out-values them — every land drop is damage, cards and bodies; Genemorph 6/6s and cat tokens go wide; the auras make the Spider bigger than anything they deploy.
Control: Niv-Mizzet and Tatyova refill after sweepers; Fae Flight and Fungal Fortitude blank spot removal; the Spider draws a card per targeting, so removal is a losing trade; the landfall burn kills through a clear board since lands can’t be countered.

title: Requiem Mass
text:
Game plan in three phases

Build the choir (turns 1-3). Deploy endure creatures and choose “create Spirit” on their triggers. Descendant of Storms attacks and makes a 1/1 Spirit for {1}{W}. Fortress Kin-Guard endures on entry. Krumar Initiate sits ready as a repeatable spirit factory.
Direct the requiem (turns 3-5). Resolve Anafenza, Unyielding Lineage and a sacrifice outlet. Start sacrificing: nontoken creatures grow Anafenza by +2/+2 (or add a 2/2 Spirit), tokens keep the draw engines fed, and Vein Ripper bleeds the opponent for 2 life per death.
Close the service. Attack with a 10/10-plus Anafenza or Hei Bai, Spirit of Balance through Rogue's Passage, or drain out with repeated sacrifices and Treacherous Greed.

title: Requiem Mass
text:
Curve and mana
Nineteen of the nonland cards cost two or less and only two cost more than three (the Vein Ripper pair), so the deck curves out aggressively and floods the board with bodies before the engine turns on. Bleachbone Verge needs a Plains or Swamp to tap for either color, so the eight basics guarantee it is live from turn one.

title: Requiem Mass
text:
Early game (turns 1-3)
Lead with Descendant of Storms or Fortress Kin-Guard. Always take the Spirit token from endure triggers in the first turns — the board presence threatens damage while quietly banking sacrifice fodder. Krumar Initiate is the best turn-two play when you expect a long game: every spare mana becomes an X/X Spirit at sorcery speed, paying life you will win back from Vein Ripper, Baron Bertram Graywater, and Treacherous Greed.

title: Requiem Mass
text:
Mid game (turns 4-6)
Land Anafenza, Unyielding Lineage and start the engine. The key sequencing rule: sacrifice nontoken creatures while Anafenza is out (each one makes her +2/+2 or a 2/2 Spirit), and sacrifice tokens when you only need cards or life. Ruthless Lawbringer is removal and an engine in one: it enters, eats a creature, and destroys any nonland permanent — with Anafenza on board the eaten creature grows her at the same time. Social Snub clears a blocker or a hexproof threat from every opponent and gains a life per copy.

title: Requiem Mass
text:
The combo turn
With Anafenza, Unyielding Lineage and Bartolomé del Presidio on the battlefield, plus any nontoken creature and a token generator:

Sacrifice the nontoken creature to Bartolomé: Bartolomé grows +1/+1, Anafenza endures 2.
Repeat with each body: Krumar Initiate can be tapped to make an X/X Spirit first, then sacrificed as a nontoken creature on a later activation, or kept alive to keep generating.
Each death also triggers Vein Ripper for 2 damage if he is out.
When Anafenza (or Bartolomé, or Hei Bai) has enough counters, activate Rogue's Passage and attack for lethal through any board.

Hei Bai, Spirit of Balance is the second engine that attacks: enter or attack, sacrifice a Spirit token, put two counters on it. A single Hei Bai attacking every turn while churning tokens through the outlet grows by +2/+2 per turn and beats as a 7/7 or larger fly-over blocker-free threat. When it finally leaves, its counters move onto your next attacker, so the growth is never wasted.

title: Requiem Mass
text:
Win condition 2: Vein Ripper drain
Vein Ripper turns the whole engine into a life-drain combo. Every creature death — tokens included — makes the opponent lose 2 life and you gain 2. A single engine turn with four or five sacrifices (Spirits from Krumar, an enduring creature, a lawbringer snack) is 8 to 10 damage. The 6/5 flying body with ward-sacrifice also ends games on its own, and Treacherous Greed closes: sacrifice a creature that already dealt combat damage this turn to draw three, drain 3, and gain 3 in one instant.

title: Requiem Mass
text:
Mulligan guide
Keep any hand with two or three lands and a two-drop. Fortress Kin-Guard or Bartolomé del Presidio on turn two is the ideal start; Anafenza in the opening seven is excellent but not required. Throw back hands full of three-drops with no early creature, hands with five or more lands, or hands with Vein Ripper and no black sources. Rogue's Passage alone does not count as a colored source in the opener.

title: Requiem Mass
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Anafenza only sees nontoken deaths. Tokens are fuel for outlets and draw; nontoken creatures are the ones that grow her. Sequence accordingly: make a Spirit, sacrifice the Spirit to Vampiric Rites for a card, then sacrifice a nontoken body to Bartolomé for the endure trigger.
Endure is a choice. “Put counters on it or create a Spirit.” You may split decisions per trigger — counters when building a voltron kill, Spirits when you need fodder or blockers.
Krumar Initiate’s activation is sorcery-speed and costs life; the X/X Spirit it makes can be sacrificed the same turn, but only after the activation resolves.
Sandbender Scavengers reanimates on its own death for a creature with mana value equal to or less than its power. Feed it counters by sacrificing other permanents, then when it dies it returns your Anafenza or Vein Ripper from the graveyard.
Ruthless Lawbringer’s destroy is optional but the sacrifice is not: when it enters you may sacrifice a creature, and only if you do does the destroy trigger go on the stack.
Vein Ripper’s ward asks for a sacrifice — your opponent pays it by losing a creature, which triggers the drain anyway. Ward here is often a free 2 damage.
Social Snub copies if you control a creature when you cast it, so it usually hits each opponent once (or twice in a mirror of two players) for an edict plus a drain.

title: Requiem Mass
text:
Matchups

Aggro: You are the control deck. Trade endure creatures, use the life gain from Rites and Ripper, and stabilize behind Vein Ripper’s 6/5 flying body. Shadowy Backstreet’s surveil finds answers.
Midrange: The engine out-values most fair decks — every removal spell they spend on your creatures is another Anafenza trigger and another drain from Ripper. Press the sacrifice loop every turn.
Control: Play around sweepers by keeping the voltron plan in hand until the turn you kill: grow Anafenza with activations, hold Rogue's Passage, and go over the top. Social Snub and Lawbringer answer their planeswalkers; ward on Vein Ripper taxes their spot removal.

title: Lifespark
text:
Overview
Lifespark fuses two build-around mechanics: Prowess (creatures grow whenever you cast a noncreature spell) and Infusion (Tarkir Dragonstorm bonuses that activate “if you gained life this turn”). The deck is a spell-slinger engine: gain a little life, then ride a chain of cheap instants and sorceries that pump every creature on the board while arming your Infusion payoffs.
The engine is Bria, Riptide Rogue: she grants prowess to every other creature you control, so even tokens, mana dorks, and animated manlands grow with each spell, and every noncreature spell also makes one of your creatures unblockable. Firebending Student turns power into red mana on attack, letting a big turn snowball: pump, attack for mana, cast more spells, pump again. Sokka, Tenacious Tactician turns each noncreature spell into a 1/1 Ally that itself has prowess, doubling the swarm. Life gain (gainlands, Lightning Helix, lifelink, Luminollusk) arms the green Infusion suite: Efflorescence becomes a +2/+2 trample-and-indestructible pump, and Lumaret’s Favor copies itself.

title: Lifespark
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Play a two-drop prowess creature on turn two (Emberheart Challenger, Firebending Student, Stormcatch Mentor, or Brightblade Stoat) or a gainland to pre-arm Infusion. Hold Lightning Strike for blockers or planeswalkers. If you have a gainland, sequence it before your first spell so Efflorescence and Lumaret’s Favor are infused.


Mid game
Resolve Bria as early as possible; she is the force multiplier. After that, every noncreature spell grows the entire team, so even a Lightning Helix pointed at a blocker grows your attackers. Sokka and Queen Brahne convert spells into board presence: Sokka’s Ally tokens have prowess twice over (Sokka’s aura plus Bria), and Brahne’s Wizards deal 1 to each opponent per spell, which doubles as reach.


The combo turn
With Bria and Firebending Student on board: attack with Student, adding red mana equal to its power (already boosted by previous spells). Use that mana plus Stormcatch Mentor’s discount to cast a chain of pump and burn spells. Each spell triggers every prowess creature, growing Student for more mana and making a creature unblockable via Bria. Finish by animating Restless Ridgeline (itself a prowess creature under Bria) and attacking with unblockable, infused, indestructible creatures.


Win condition 2: burn reach
When the board stalls, convert it into damage: sacrifice a prowess-pumped Heartfire Immolator for damage equal to its power; chain Lightning Strike and Lightning Helix (discounted by Mentor); let Queen Brahne tokens ping each opponent every time you cast a spell. Lightning Helix doubles as the life gain that keeps Infusion armed while burning.


Mulligan guide
Keep any hand with two to three lands (at least one red source and one blue or green source) and a two-drop prowess creature or Bria. Mulligan hands with four or more lands, no creatures, or no way to reach three mana by turn three. Bria plus any two spells is a strong keep.


Key interactions and edge cases

Infusion checks “if you gained life this turn” at resolution, so any life gain earlier in the turn works, including a gainland played that same turn.
Bria’s unblockable ability targets a creature each time you cast a noncreature spell; multiple spells can make multiple creatures unblockable.
Efflorescence’s indestructible saves a creature from the damage of your own Lightning Strike or from blockers, but not from sacrifice effects.
Firebending Student’s mana expires at end of combat; spend it in the second main phase.
Comforting Counsel counts every life gain event, including lifelink damage and each gainland.



Matchups

Aggro: The lifegain package (Stoat, Helix, Luminollusk, gainlands) buys time; infused Efflorescence creates an indestructible blocker; Withering-Curse-style sweeps are not needed if you race.
Control: Cavern of Souls protects Bria and Thor from counterspells; Emberheart Challenger and Mentor apply early pressure; Bria’s unblockable ability punches through removal-heavy boards.
Midrange: The combo turn outgrows most midrange boards; keep Lightning Strike for their must-answer creature and win the race.

title: The Rewritten Stampede
text:
Overview
The Rewritten Stampede fuses three mechanics into one engine: Saddle mounts attack for value, Convoke spells are cast by tapping the same creatures, and Plan enchantments count every tap. The heart of the deck is Rewrite History: whenever one or more creatures you control become tapped, you draw a card, discard a card, and advance the plan. Attacking, saddling, convoking, and even Station all tap creatures — so every axis of the deck draws cards.
The other two Plans turn the same actions into resources. Death to Our Enemies makes a Treasure for every noncreature spell you cast (all your Convoke spells), which ramps the deck into its 5-6 mana finishers, and caps at 7 damage. Political Triumph turns every creature that enters into scry 1 plus a plan counter, ending in a global +1/+1 anthem.
The payoff is a go-wide Mount army. Seraphic Steed mints 3/3 flying Angels each saddled attack, Bridled Bighorn adds Sheep, Bounding Felidar pumps the whole team, Drover Grizzly gives trample, and Collective Inferno doubles all damage dealt by Mounts. Dracosaur Auxiliary swings in the air with haste and shocks anything. Games end in one massive, doubled, trampling stampede — or a 7-point burn finish.

Gameplay strategy

Early game
Mulligan for Rewrite History plus any 1-2 drop Mount or Political Triumph. A turn-1 Political Triumph followed by creatures scries every draw step. Gilded Ghoda is the best early Mount: 2/2, saddle 1, and every saddled attack makes a Treasure — ramp and card draw on one body. Seraphic Steed (2/2 first strike, lifelink) races aggro while it waits for saddle 4.


Mid game
Land Death to Our Enemies and start casting Convoke spells — each one makes a Treasure. Unswerving Sloth is the engine-breaker: saddle it (tap 4 power), attack, and it untaps every creature you control, setting up a free main-phase Convoke turn. Guardian Sunmare tutors any nonland permanent with mana value 3 or less on a saddled attack — fetch a second copy of a Plan, another Mount, or a Convoke spell.


The combo turn

Have a wide board of Mounts and at least Collective Inferno (Mount).
Main phase 1: tap Pilots and tokens to saddle Dracosaur Auxiliary (saddle 3), Bounding Felidar (saddle 2) and Guardian Sunmare (saddle 4). Every tap draws a card off Rewrite History and every noncreature spell cast so far made a Treasure.
Attack: Dracosaur flies over for 4 (8 with Inferno) plus 2-4 shock damage; Felidar puts a +1/+1 counter on every other creature and gains life; Drover Grizzly grants trample; Seraphic Steed mints 3/3 Angels; lifelink keeps you ahead.
Main phase 2: Harmonized Crescendo (choose Mount) draws a card per Mount permanent — routinely 8-12 cards — or Unexpected Assistance digs deeper. Rewrite History then returns the best instants/sorceries from the graveyard to hand for the next loop.

A fully developed board deals 25-40 doubled, trampling damage in one swing.


Win condition 2: burn and grind
Death to Our Enemies reaches four plan counters after four noncreature spells (Plans, Convoke spells, and lands’ activated abilities do not count — spells only). That is easy with this shell: the payoff is 7 damage split as you choose, usually 7 to the face to finish after one stampede. In grindy games, Rewrite History recurs Temporal Cleansing, Appeal to Eirdu, and Unexpected Assistance, while Harmonized Crescendo refills the hand off the Mount count.


Mulligan guide
Keep: any hand with Rewrite History or Political Triumph plus 2-3 lands and a creature. Keep 2-land hands only with a 1-2 drop Mount (Gilded Ghoda, Seraphic Steed). Ship: hands without a Mount or a Plan, and hands flooded with 5-6 mana spells. Bucolic Ranch is a strong keep — it fixes and finds the finishers.


Key interactions and edge cases

Rewrite History triggers on any tap: attacking, saddling, convoking, and Station taps all draw. Plan the order — saddle first, then convoke, so each tap draws.
Pilots saddle as power 3: one Pilot covers saddle 1-3; two Pilots cover saddle 4 (Seraphic Steed, Guardian Sunmare, Unswerving Sloth).
The Wandering Rescuer protects tapped creatures with hexproof and blocks with flash, double strike — cast it with Convoke at instant speed.
Temporal Cleansing answers anything nonland, including indestructible threats (it tucks instead of destroying).
Adagia copies an enchantment at 12+ charge counters: copying Collective Inferno quadruples Mount damage; copying a Plan re-runs its payoff.
Death to Our Enemies cares about spells, not abilities: saddling and Station do not advance it, Convoke spells and Plans do.



Matchups

Aggro: Seraphic Steed’s lifelink, The Wandering Rescuer’s flash blocks, and Bounding Felidar’s lifegain stabilize; stall until the stampede.
Control: Death to Our Enemies ramps you through counterspells (Treasures are instant-speed mana), Rewrite History restocks after board wipes, and hexproof from The Wandering Rescuer protects tapped attackers.
Midrange: out-muscle with Angels, trample, and doubled damage; Temporal Cleansing removes the single biggest blocker.

Scavenger’s Talent converts deaths into Food tokens, Demand Answers and Eaten Alive spend those tokens on cards and removal, and Ruthless Lawbringer trades any creature for any nonland permanent.
The fodder never runs out. Bonebind Orator and Unstoppable Slasher return from the graveyard, Cauldron of Essence reanimates one creature per activation, Raise the Past floods back every 2-mana-value creature, and Hop to It, Kambal (token copies via Three Steps Ahead) and Great Arashin City keep tokens flowing. Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubles the entire drain package on your turn, turning a modest loop into a kill.

Three Steps Ahead can copy any of your creatures into a token, which then triggers Kambal and feeds the sacrifice engine.

Overview
Mirkwood Menagerie is the ninth dedicated daily Hobbit combo deck. Eight earlier builds claimed the set’s headline engines — the storied dwarves, the goblin amass raid, the elvenking’s court, Smaug’s hoard, the wilderland pack, the Lake-town recruits, the dwarf bards and the thieves of the crooked way — so today’s deck takes the wild remnants of the set and makes them cohere: wolves, bears, a rabbit, a bee, Mirkwood elves, an eagle and a border garrison. The unused Hobbit pool is thin (18 cards, all common/uncommon), so the deck is fused around the two mechanics those leftovers share: Ferocious (Rabbit and Warg pay off power 4 or greater) and Landfall (Raft-Steerer and the Mirkwood druids trigger off every land), held together by a +1/+1 counter subtheme and a token-swarm finish.
The engine chain is simple but deep: small creatures (and the tokens they make) draw cards through Enduring Innocence; big creatures (Ordinary Bear, a pumped Guardian of the Halls, a grown Elvish Refueler, Ojer Taq) draw cards through Outcaster Trailblazer; Mirkwood Nurturer bounces a creature or land to re-trigger entries and landfall; and every creature on the board feeds Esgaroth Garrison’s power. Then Ojer Taq, Deepest Foundation triples every token — soldiers, heroes and roles — and Zanarkand’s adventure lands a Hero token with a +1/+1 counter for each land you control.

title: Landwarp
text:
Overview
Landwarp fuses three mechanics into one combat engine. Landfall turns every land drop into power and board growth (Tifa Lockhart doubles her power, Mossborn Hydra doubles its counters, Mightform Harmonizer doubles any creature’s power, Eusocial Engineering and Felidar Retreat add bodies). Warp is the recursion half: every warp card can be cast from hand for a discount, is exiled at the next end step, and can be cast again from exile on a later turn, so engines like Mightform Harmonizer and Eusocial Engineering keep returning. Sneak is the surprise-attack half: when you have an unblocked attacker, you return it to hand during the declare blockers step and cast a Sneak card for its sneak cost — creatures enter tapped and attacking, which is how Michelangelo, Improviser lands on the board mid-combat and starts dumping lands and creatures from your hand.
The three mechanics reinforce each other. Michelangelo’s combat damage trigger plays an extra land and an extra creature, which feeds Landfall payoffs on the same turn they attack. Raphael, the Nightwatcher gives all attackers double strike, so a Landfall-doubled Tifa or Hydra ends games in one swing. Dark Leo and Shredder turn the ninja count into a second, independent kill: every combat with five or more Ninjas (turtles and spirit tokens included) makes the opponent lose half their remaining life.

title: Landwarp

Approach

Game plan by phase
Early game (T1-T3). Develop: Sazh’s Chocobo, Tifa Lockhart, Splinter (menace gives you unblocked attackers), and an engine (Mightform Harmonizer, Eusocial Engineering via warp, Felidar Retreat). Play a land every turn; every landfall trigger is a pump or a token. Hold combat tricks (Shredder’s Technique) for must-kill blockers.
Mid game (T4-T5). Start the sneak turns. Attack with a menace ninja or an evasive token; if it goes unblocked, return it to hand during declare blockers and cast a Sneak card for its cost: Michelangelo (drops land and creature from hand), Oroku Saki (draws), Dark Leo and Shredder (makes a Ninja token), or The Last Ronin’s Technique (three Spirit tokens, tapped and attacking when sneaked).
The combo turn. With Michelangelo and Raphael plus a landfall engine in play: attack, sneak Michelangelo in tapped and attacking, his damage trigger puts a land and a creature from hand onto the battlefield, the land triggers every Landfall payoff (Tifa, Hydra, Harmonizer, Eusocial robots, Felidar cat), Raphael makes the whole team double strike, and Restless Cottage or a Robot token closes.

The manabase is 24 lands: eleven basics for the verge conditions, six verge duals covering every color pair, Restless Cottage, and four fetch lands that double as landfall triggers. title: Landwarp
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Prioritize land drops over everything: Sazh’s Chocobo and Tifa Lockhart grow on every landfall, so the first three turns are about curving lands and cheap green threats. Splinter, Hamato Yoshi is the best two-drop: menace is your most reliable source of unblocked attackers for sneak costs, and it pumps the other Ninjas. If the opener has a warp engine (Mightform Harmonizer or Eusocial Engineering), warp-cast it cheaply: it will be exiled at end step and come back next turn, giving a second round of landfall triggers.


Mid game
Set up the kill: keep an engine on the board, hold a land in hand for Michelangelo, and attack with the ninja package. Do not overextend into sweepers; All-Fates Stalker and Shredder’s Technique keep the opponent’s blockers and bombs honest, and Splinter’s Technique fetches exactly the piece the board state needs.


The combo turn

Attack with a ninja or menace creature.
If it is unblocked, return it to hand in the declare blockers step and cast Michelangelo, Improviser for its sneak cost {2}{G}{G}; he enters tapped and attacking.
Michelangelo’s combat damage lets you put a creature card and/or a land card from hand onto the battlefield.
The extra land drop fires every Landfall ability: Tifa and Hydra double, Mightform doubles another creature’s power, Eusocial makes a Robot, Felidar Retreat makes a Cat or pumps the team.
With Raphael, the Nightwatcher also attacking, all attackers have double strike; Restless Cottage and Robots add the final points.



Win condition 2: the ninja swarm
Dark Leo and Shredder creates a 1/1 Ninja token every time it deals combat damage, and each such trigger checks the ninja count: if you control five or more Ninjas, the opponent loses half their life, rounded up. Turtles and Splinter are Ninjas, The Last Ronin’s Technique’s three Spirits are Ninja Turtle Spirits, and every Dark Leo hit adds another token, so two solid combat steps with the swarm end the game regardless of the landfall math.


Mulligan guide
Keep any hand with two or three lands and a cheap threat (Sazh’s Chocobo, Tifa, Splinter). Keep hands with a warp engine plus enough lands to cast it or warp it by turn three. Ship hands that are all four-drops or missing color sources for their early cards; the deck wants to use its lands every turn.


Key interactions and edge cases

Sneak requires an unblocked attacker: if your only attacker is blocked, you cannot pay sneak costs that turn. Menace (Splinter) and evasive tokens are the safety valves.
Warped permanents are exiled at the beginning of the next end step and can be cast from exile later, so warp is not a one-shot discount: it is a repeatable engine, and warp costs can be paid again each turn.
All-Fates Stalker exiles a non-Assassin creature until it leaves the battlefield; warp-casting it each turn gives repeatable exile removal.
Michelangelo’s trigger is optional (“you may”), and you can choose only a creature, only a land, or both.
The Last Ronin’s Technique’s Spirits enter tapped and attacking only when the sneak cost was paid; cast normally they are just three chump-blockers/attackers.
Weftstalker Ardent pings each opponent for every creature or artifact that enters under your control, so token-making turns (Eusocial Robots, Felidar Cats, Dark Leo Ninjas, Last Ronin Spirits) double as reach.
Shredder’s Technique destroys enchantments too, and you lose 2 life only if it destroys an enchantment.



Matchups
Against aggro, block early with Felidar Retreat Cats and Sazh’s Chocobo, and use Shredder’s Technique and Jennika-style tempo to stabilize; lifegain from Restless Cottage Food and the Cat token race matters. Against midrange, warp recursion out-values them: engines keep coming back from exile while their one-for-one removal runs dry. Against control, spread the clock: Ninja tokens and Restless Cottage survive sweepers as lands, Splinter’s Technique finds the finisher, and Raphael plus double strike punishes tapped-out turns. The deck’s weakness is fast combo and wide flyer strategies, where the manabase’s tapped fetch lands cost a tempo turn.

title: Sunstar Vigil
text:
Overview
Sunstar Vigil fuses three build-around mechanics into one engine. Station (the Edge of Eternities mechanic) lets you tap a creature to put charge counters equal to its power on a Spacecraft or Planet, unlocking thresholds that turn your artifacts and lands into flying, lifelink, damage-dealing machines. Lifegain is the fuel: every life you gain powers Amalia’s explores, Exemplar of Light’s counters, and keeps you alive while your ships charge. Solved (the Case mechanic) provides the payoff layer: Case of the Shattered Pact solves off the five planets’ colors alone and turns any attacker into a flying double-striker, while Case of the Gorgon’s Kiss solves off your own milling and deaths into a 4/4 lifelink deathtouch creature.
Every card feeds the loop: high-power creatures (Vaultborn Tyrant, The Seriema) both gain life and charge Station; spacecraft draw cards and recur each other; the Planets are lands that become engines at 12+ charges, including the deck’s win-condition land, Adagia.

title: Sunstar Vigil
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Prioritize a 2-drop: Lumen-Class Frigate (it becomes an anthem at just 2 charges), Case of the Shattered Pact (fixes mana), or Wurmwall Sweeper (surveils toward your combo). The Seriema is the best turn-3 play: it finds Aurelia against race-y decks and Amalia when you need the wipe. Do not tap creatures to Station unless you are sure they will survive; the Seriema’s indestructible clause protects tapped legendaries, which makes charging with her safe.


Mid game and the combo turn
Chain lifegain triggers: Vaultborn Tyrant entering (gain 3, draw), Exemplar of Light growing on every lifegain event, Fell Gravship and Gorgon’s Kiss gaining life when they deal combat damage. Each trigger makes Amalia explore, growing her toward 20. When Amalia hits exactly 20 power, all other creatures are destroyed, and if the Pact is solved she attacks with flying and double strike for 40.
The Dawnsire line needs only 10 charges: tap Vaultborn Tyrant (6) and The Seriema (5) on a sorcery turn, then swing with anything, or animate Dawnsire with Case of the Filched Falcon for a 4/4 flying attacker that still pings 100. Aurelia’s extra combat phase untaps your team and triggers Dawnsire again; Adagia copying Dawnsire doubles both the pings and the 20/20 flyers.


Win condition #2 (spacecraft beatdown)
If Amalia is answered, the ships close the game: Sledge-Class Seedship cheats Vaultborn Tyrant into play on attack, robots from Wedgelight Rammer grow under Lumen’s anthem, and Kavaron’s haste anthem plus Aurelia’s extra combat turn any board into lethal. Dawnsire’s pings remove every blocker and opposing planeswalker first.


Mulligan guide
Keep: three or more lands with two colors, any 2-drop, The Seriema. Ship: one-landers, five-color hands with only tapped trilands and no 2-drop, hands with nothing but seven-drops.


Key interactions and edge cases

Station is a sorcery: you cannot charge in response to combat tricks.
Amalia’s wipe destroys all other creatures, including yours; plan to keep the spacecraft (they are artifacts) and the solved Gorgon’s Kiss (an enchantment) out of the blast radius.
The wipe puts many creature cards into graveyards, which solves Gorgon’s Kiss the same turn.
Vaultborn Tyrant’s death creates an artifact token copy; it is both Station fodder and a sacrifice for Susur Secundi.
Stroke of Midnight’s 1/1 Human token is extra sacrifice fodder; the token also gives you a creature to tap for Station.
Shattered Pact solves at end step once five colors are among permanents you control; the five Planets alone satisfy it.



Matchups

Aggro: Elspeth’s Smite exiles their attackers, Lumen’s anthem stalls the ground, and lifegain outpaces their burn. Solved Gorgon’s Kiss is a 4/4 lifelink wall.
Midrange: Out-grind with Vaultborn Tyrant draws and Susur Secundi’s power-based card draw; Dawnsire clears their best creatures every turn.
Control: Ward on Amalia taxes their counters, Planets are lands and dodge sweepers, and the solved Pact turns any surviving creature into a flying double-striker after a wipe.
Combo mirrors: Stroke of Midnight removes their enchantments and planeswalkers; Dawnsire’s 100-damage pings kill their combo creatures on sight.

Mid game
Start sacrificing on your own terms. Fanatical Offering turns any skeleton into two cards and a Map token; Worthy Cost answers a planeswalker or creature for one mana plus a body that was going to die anyway. Every nontoken death triggers Midnight Reaper, so a single Reassembling Skeleton recursion loop is a repeatable draw spell. Corpseberry Cultivator forages at every combat — exile three graveyard cards (or sacrifice a Food from a Cottage attack) to grow it into a credible Teamwork contributor.


The combo turn
The board is a committee of 2-power skeletons and a Restless Cottage. Tap total power 4 (two 2/2 Miners, or Miner + Bloodghast, or the 4/4 Cottage) to pay Teamwork on Too Evil to Stay Dead and reanimate two of Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Rune-Scarred Demon and Enduring Tenacity from the graveyard you have been filling all game. Demon tutors the missing piece; then the drain loop closes:

Attack with Restless Cottage — it creates a Food token.
Sacrifice the Food: gain 3 life.
Enduring Tenacity: target opponent loses 3 life.
Bloodthirsty Conqueror: you gain 3 life — loop back to step 3. The opponent dies.

The loop needs only Conqueror + Tenacity + any lifegain, and both halves are reanimation targets, so the graveyard is the hand. If the loop is disrupted, the reanimated pair still attacks for 10-11 flying damage with the Demon’s tutor finding whatever is missing.

Keep any hand with two or three lands and a one- or two-drop — the deck functions on skeletons alone. Ship hands with no black source or with only tapped lands and no early play. Keep Too Evil to Stay Dead plus a sacrifice spell plus a body; the reanimation plan only needs a graveyard, which sacrifice provides. Against aggressive decks, favor removal (Worthy Cost, HULK SMASH!) over the Teamwork spells.

Crime recursion: Worthy Cost, Cruel Alliance, Repulsor Blast and HULK SMASH!’s fight mode all target opponents or their permanents, so each one recurs Forsaken Miner for {B} — sequence removal before combat to rebuild the board for Teamwork.
Teamwork is optional: every Teamwork spell can be cast without tapping — a doubled mode is a bonus, not a requirement; tap only when the payoff is worth the tapped creatures.
Enduring Tenacity returns as an enchantment when it dies as a creature — it stops being sacrifice fodder but keeps draining, so the combo survives a board wipe.
Too Evil to Stay Dead without Teamwork is still a two-for-one enabler at mana value 4 or less — Solemn Simulacrum is the ideal cheap target (ramps, then draws on death).
Fountainport tokens count: a 1/1 Fish is a creature for Teamwork 1 and a sacrifice for Fanatical Offering, and sacrificing it draws a card.
Don’t over-sacrifice: the team is also the Teamwork payment; keep at least one body untapped to pay Teamwork 2/4 next turn.

Aggro: the skeletons block forever and Worthy Cost / HULK SMASH! / Cruel Alliance clear the path; Conqueror’s lifegain ends the race.
Midrange: grind them out — every sacrifice replaces itself with cards (Fanatical Offering, Midnight Reaper) while Too Evil reanimates bigger creatures than they can answer.
Control: spread threats (manlands, Fountainport Fish) so sweepers never fully reset; the graveyard is a second hand, so wraths that don’t exile are meaningless. Rogue’s Passage closes through blockers.
Graveyard hate: the deck still plays a fair midrange game — skeletons and removal — but mulligan aggressively for Cottage plus Team Tactics to win on the land plan instead.

title: Chromatic Caper

Overview
Chromatic Caper fuses three build-around mechanics: Vivid (effects scale with X, the number of colors among permanents you control), Plot (pay a small cost to exile a card, then cast it later without paying its mana cost), and Alliance (creatures that trigger whenever another creature enters under your control). The deck is a five-color plot-combo engine: plot spells cheaply on turns two through four, then dump them for free in a single explosive turn. Every free creature triggers every Alliance creature, and every colored permanent you resolve pushes Vivid’s X toward the full five colors.
The engine is Fblthp, Lost on the Range, who gives the top card of your library plot and lets you plot nonland cards from the top of your library, and Make Your Own Luck, which plots a card and puts the other two into your hand. Bloom Tender is the mana core: with five colors among your permanents it taps for five mana, letting a plotted top end cast for free on the same turn you untap. Outcaster Trailblazer fixes mana on entry and draws a card whenever a 4+ power creature enters, which the free Freestrider Commandos (5/5 when cast without paying) and Slash (7/5) trigger constantly.
The kill is the fusion working at once. Slash, Reptile Rampager deals 2 damage to each opponent for every creature that enters, and creates a 2/2 Mutant token when it attacks, which enters and pings again. Meanwhile Squawkroaster grows to 5 power with five colors, and Glister Bairn hands it +5/+5 at combat, making a 10/4 double striker. Rogue’s Passage makes that creature unblockable, and Shimmercreep drains for 5 as a finisher.

Slash’s attack token enters after combat begins; its Alliance triggers resolve before damage, so the ping can finish an opponent before blockers are declared.

Balin, Bifur, or the Staff in the opener is a gift, not a requirement. Mulligan one-land hands and hands with five or more lands and no two-drop. title: Hearth and Hammer

Key interactions and edge cases

Storied counts artifacts, legendaries, and Sagas among permanents you control — Equipment tokens from Blacksmith and Dáin Ironfoot count, and the enduring story, once gained, lasts for the rest of the game even if the board empties.
Balin’s trigger is optional (“you may discard your hand”) — with an empty hand, X is zero and there is no damage; always loot or play a Dwarf maker before resolving Balin triggers.
Bifur and Wizard’s Staff are separate replacement effects — both apply, so a Dwarf trigger fires three times, not four.
Kíli’s draw is once per turn; Wizard’s Staff on Kíli (rather than Balin) doubles that draw to two, but the Staff belongs on Balin on the kill turn.
At the Door tokens are Dwarves — each one triggers Balin, Kíli, and Fíli; they also count for Dáin Ironfoot’s double strike if the game goes to combat.
Wizard’s Staff’s “Equip Wizard {1}” only applies to Wizards; equipping it to Balin costs {3} — or {0} as Kíli’s first equip of the turn.
Glamdring’s cost reduction scales with the equipped creature’s power — a 6-power Dwarf makes Vow to Erebor, Thorin’s Last Stand, and Gleam of Death free.
Cavern of Souls mana only casts Dwarf creature spells — never use it for Vow to Erebor or At the Door.
The Lonely Mountain enters tapped without an Equipment — sequence your artifacts before your lands on turn 1-2.
Roads Go Ever, Ever On exiles Plains rather than putting them onto the battlefield — it fixes by returning them to hand, and its chapter IV pump counts Plains you control at that moment.
